children: Crude oil contracts were trading higher around midday Wednesday, on track to extend their gains to a third straight day, as renewed attacks between the U.S. and Iran dashed hopes of a deal to restart critical Middle East petroleum supplies any time soon.
At 11:45 a.m. ET, NYMEX October West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up around 65cts to $90.85/bbl, the highest in more than a month. November WTI was up 45cts to $88.20/bbl.
London-based October Brent was $1.05 higher to $95.70/bbl and November Brent was up 45cts to $92.05/bbl.
The oil benchmarks have gained about $6-$7 on lingering fears over the six-month-old Middle East conflicts that have halted vital crude and petroleum exports to the rest of the world.

Diesel prices took a breather after Tuesday's sharp rally. October ULSD was up 1.55ct to $4.6885/gal, while November ULSD was down 0.4ct to $4.5015/gal. October RBOB was up 0.5ct to $3.14/gal and November RBOB was 0.2cts higher to $2.9685/gal.

The energy market is now digesting the latest Energy Information Administration data that showed U.S. crude oil and gasoline inventories fell last week, even as demand declined. Meanwhile, distillate inventories saw a small increase during the week ending Friday.
